State Bank of India - Probationary Officer Examination
About the Examination

The State Bank of India (SBI) Probationary Officer (PO) Examination is one of the most prestigious and competitive banking exams in India. Conducted annually by the SBI, it recruits candidates for the junior management level position of Probationary Officer (Scale-I). An SBI PO career is highly sought-after for its excellent remuneration, job security, rapid growth prospects, and the opportunity to work in India's largest public sector bank.
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination
The SBI PO exam is designed to select dynamic and capable individuals who can be nurtured into future leaders of the bank. The selection process aims to identify candidates with:
Analytical & Decision-Making Skills: The ability to analyze complex data, interpret financial information, and make sound judgments under pressure.
Problem-Solving Aptitude: Strong logical reasoning and quantitative skills to tackle banking-related challenges.
Communication & Interpersonal Skills: The ability to communicate effectively, manage customer relationships, and work in a team.
General & Economic Awareness: A comprehensive understanding of the banking industry, national economy, and current affairs.
🏦 The Role of a Probationary Officer
🪜 The Three-Phase Selection Process
The SBI PO selection is a rigorous three-stage process designed to thoroughly evaluate a candidate's suitability.

Phase 1: Preliminary Examination (The Screening Test): This is an online, objective-type screening test. Its purpose is purely to shortlist a reasonable number of candidates for the Main examination. The marks obtained in the Prelims are not counted for the final merit list .

Phase 2: Main Examination (The Merit Decider): This is the most crucial stage. It consists of both an objective test and a descriptive test. The scores from the Main examination are used for shortlisting candidates for the final phase and are also a major component of the final merit list.

Phase 3: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview (The Personality Assessment): Candidates who clear the Mains undergo a Psychometric Test (to assess personality), followed by a Group Exercise and a personal Interview. This phase evaluates a candidate's communication skills, leadership qualities, and overall personality.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Selection

The final merit list is prepared by aggregating the marks obtained in the Main Examination (Phase 2) and the Group Exercise & Interview (Phase 3) . The scores are normalized to 100. Candidates are selected from the top of this merit list based on their category and the number of vacancies.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)
The SBI PO recruitment cycle typically completes within 6-7 months from notification to the final result. The following is a general, indicative schedule.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official SBI notification for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (September - October)
September: The official notification for the PO Examination is released by SBI on its careers website (sbi.co.in/web/careers).
September - October: The online application window opens and remains active for about three weeks . Candidates are required to register, fill the form, and pay the fee.
Phase 2: Preliminary Examination (November)
October / November: Approximately 10-15 days before the exam , SBI releases the call letter (admit card) for the Preliminary Examination.
November: The Preliminary Examination is conducted online in multiple shifts over several days.
November / December: The result of the Prelims is declared, usually within 2-3 weeks.
Phase 3: Main Examination (December)
December: Call letters for the Main Examination are released for all candidates shortlisted from the Prelims.
December: The Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) is conducted online on a single day.
January: The result of the Main Examination is declared.
Phase 4: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview (January - February)
January / February: Call letters for Phase 3 are issued to candidates who clear the Mains cut-off.
February: The Psychometric Test, Group Exercises, and Interviews are conducted at various centers across the country.
Phase 5: Final Result (February - March)
February / March: The final result, containing the list of selected candidates, is declared by SBI. The joining process begins shortly after.
Eligibility Criteria
Candidates must ensure they fulfill all the eligibility criteria stipulated by SBI. Eligibility is determined by Nationality, Age Limit, Educational Qualification, and the Number of Attempts.
⚠️ Note: The details provided are general. Always verify from the official SBI PO notification for the current year, as it is the final authority.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate must be a citizen of India.
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age of the candidate is calculated as of a specific cut-off date, typically the 1st of April of the recruitment year.
Age Limit: Not below 21 years and not above 30 years .
For example, for the 2025 exam, a candidate must have been born not earlier than 02.04.1995 and not later than 01.04.2004 (both days inclusive).
Relaxations in the upper age limit are provided for reserved categories:
🎓 3. Educational Qualification
The minimum educational requirement is a graduation degree.
Essential Qualification: A Graduation degree in any discipline from a recognised University or any equivalent qualification recognised as such by the Central Government.

Final-Year Students: Candidates who are in the Final Year/Semester of their Graduation may also apply provisionally, subject to the condition that, if called for an interview, they will have to produce proof of having passed the graduation examination on or before the specified cut-off date.
✍️ 4. Number of Attempts
SBI places a limit on the number of times a candidate can appear for the PO examination. Appearing in the Preliminary Exam is not counted as an attempt, but appearing in the Main Exam is counted .
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The SBI PO examination consists of three phases. A thorough understanding of the pattern is crucial for success.
🎯 Phase-I: Preliminary Examination (Qualifying)
The Prelims is an online objective test to screen candidates for the Main exam. Candidates must clear both the overall and sectional cut-offs.
Sectional Timings: Each section is timed separately for 20 minutes . Candidates cannot switch between sections.
Negative Marking: There is a penalty of 0.25 marks (1/4th of the mark assigned to the question) for each incorrect answer.
Qualifying Nature: Marks are not considered for the final merit list.
📝 Phase-II: Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive)
This is the core stage for merit calculation. It consists of an objective test and a descriptive test, both conducted online.
This test is conducted online immediately after the completion of the objective test. Candidates will have to type their answers on the computer.
Subjects: English Language (Letter Writing & Essay).
Number of Questions: 2
Maximum Marks: 50
Duration: 30 Minutes
Sectional Timings & Marks: Both timings and marks vary for each section in the objective test.
Negative Marking: A penalty of 0.25 marks applies to wrong answers in the objective test.
🗣️ Phase-III: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview
Candidates numbering up to 3 times the category-wise vacancies are shortlisted for this phase.
Psychometric Test: Conducted to assess the personality profile of the candidates. There are no marks, but the report may be used by the interview panel.
Group Exercise (GE): 20 Marks
Interview: 30 Marks
Total Marks for Phase III: 50 Marks
📊 Final Rank Calculation

The marks obtained in the Preliminary Exam (Phase-I) will not be added for preparing the final merit list for selection. Only the marks obtained in Main Examination (Phase-II) and Phase-III will be considered.
Marks from Main Exam (Objective + Descriptive) are converted out of 75 .
Marks from Group Exercise & Interview are converted out of 25 .
The final merit list is prepared based on the total score out of 100 .
Application Workflow
The application process for SBI PO is completely online via the official SBI careers website (sbi.co.in/web/careers) .
📝 Stage 1: Registration
Candidates need to register themselves on the portal by providing their basic information like name, mobile number, and email ID. A provisional registration number and password will be generated.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Application Form & Uploading Documents
Log in using the registration number and password to complete the application form.
Personal & Academic Details: Fill in all required details carefully.

Document Upload: Candidates are required to upload scanned copies of: Photograph: 4.5cm × 3.5cm, 20 KB to 50 KB. Signature (on white paper with black ink): 10 KB to 20 KB. Left Thumb Impression (on white paper with black or blue ink): 20 KB to 50 KB. Handwritten Declaration (on white paper with black ink): A specific text provided in the notification, to be written by the candidate. Size: 50 KB to 100 KB.
Photograph: 4.5cm × 3.5cm, 20 KB to 50 KB.
Signature (on white paper with black ink): 10 KB to 20 KB.
Left Thumb Impression (on white paper with black or blue ink): 20 KB to 50 KB.
Handwritten Declaration (on white paper with black ink): A specific text provided in the notification, to be written by the candidate. Size: 50 KB to 100 KB.
💳 Stage 3: Fee Payment
Amount: ₹750/- for General, EWS, and OBC candidates. NIL for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates.
₹750/- for General, EWS, and OBC candidates.
NIL for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates.
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online using Debit Card, Credit Card, or Internet Banking.
✅ Stage 4: Final Submission
Review and Submit: Preview the application form to verify all details before final submission. Once submitted, no changes can be made.
Print Application & e-Receipt: After successful payment, take a printout of the system-generated application form and the e-receipt for future reference.
⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid
Handwritten Declaration: Do not use capital letters for the entire declaration. Write it exactly as specified in the notification.
Document Specifications: Ensure all scanned documents meet the size and dimension criteria to avoid rejection.
Final Submission: Submitting the application without paying the fee (if applicable) will lead to cancellation.
Email and Mobile Number: Use a personal and active email ID and mobile number, as all communications from SBI will be sent to them.
Syllabus
The SBI PO syllabus is comprehensive and tests a candidate's aptitude for a banking career. The following is a detailed topic-wise breakdown.
📚 Part A: Preliminary Examination Syllabus

This section tests logical thinking. Key topics include: Puzzles (Floor, Box, Day/Month based), Seating Arrangements (Linear, Circular, Square), Syllogism, Inequality, Blood Relations, Direction & Distance, Coding-Decoding, Order & Ranking, and Alphanumeric Series.

This section tests numerical ability and speed. Key topics include: Data Interpretation (Bar Graph, Line Chart, Pie Chart, Tabular, Caselet), Number Series (Missing and Wrong), Simplification & Approximation, Quadratic Equations, and Arithmetic Problems (Percentage, Profit & Loss, Simple & Compound Interest, Ratio & Proportion, Time & Work, Time, Speed & Distance, Averages, Mensuration, Probability, Permutation & Combination).

This section tests grammar and comprehension skills. Key topics include: Reading Comprehension (RC), Cloze Test, Para Jumbles / Sentence Rearrangement, Error Spotting, Sentence Improvement, Fill in the Blanks (Single & Double), and Vocabulary (Synonyms, Antonyms).
✒️ Part B: Main Examination Syllabus
The Mains syllabus is an extension of the Prelims with a significantly higher difficulty level.

Reasoning: Advanced Level Puzzles and Seating Arrangements, Logical Reasoning (Statement-Assumption, Course of Action, Cause-Effect, Inference), Input-Output, Coded Syllogism & Inequality, Data Sufficiency.
Computer Aptitude: Basics of Computer Hardware & Software, Operating Systems, MS Office, Networking, Internet, and Cyber Security. (Questions are typically integrated with reasoning).

This section focuses entirely on DI. Topics include: Advanced and complex DI sets, Logical DI, Arithmetic DI, Missing Data DI. Questions from Probability, Permutation & Combination, and Mensuration are often integrated into DI sets.
This section is crucial for scoring. Topics are divided into three parts:
Current Affairs: National and International news of the last 6 months, with a focus on news related to banking and finance. Important Days, Awards, Summits, Appointments, Books & Authors.

Banking & Financial Awareness: Banking terms, History of Banking in India, Structure of Indian Banking Industry, RBI and its functions, Monetary Policy, Capital Market, Money Market, Government Schemes, Financial Institutions.
Static Awareness: Countries & Capitals, Currencies, Dams, National Parks, Stadiums, etc.
Objective: Advanced Reading Comprehension (with inferential questions), New Pattern Cloze Test, Advanced Para Jumbles, Vocabulary-based questions.
Descriptive: Essay Writing: Topics related to social issues, economy, banking, or current events. Letter Writing: Both Formal (to bank managers, editors) and Informal (to friends, family) letters.
Essay Writing: Topics related to social issues, economy, banking, or current events.
Letter Writing: Both Formal (to bank managers, editors) and Informal (to friends, family) letters.
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some common questions about the SBI PO Examination.
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Attempts

Is there a limit on the number of attempts for SBI PO? Yes. Unlike many other exams, SBI PO has a limit. General category candidates have 4 attempts. The limit is 7 for OBC candidates, and there is no restriction for SC/ST candidates. Appearing in the Main examination counts as an attempt.
What is the minimum percentage required in graduation? There is no minimum percentage requirement. A candidate only needs to have a passing degree in any discipline from a recognized university.
❓ Regarding the Examination

Are there sectional cut-offs in SBI PO? Yes. In both the Preliminary and Main examinations, candidates are required to clear not only the overall cut-off but also the sectional cut-off for each subject to be eligible for the next stage.

Can I switch between sections during the exam? No. Both Prelims and Mains have sectional timings. You can only work on a particular section for the time allotted to it. The system automatically moves to the next section once the time is over.

Are the scores of the Preliminary exam considered for the final merit list? No. The Preliminary exam is only for screening/qualifying purposes. The final merit list is based on the combined scores of the Main Examination (Phase-II) and the Group Exercise & Interview (Phase-III).
❓ Regarding Job & Career

Is there a bond period after getting selected as an SBI PO? Yes. Selected candidates are required to sign a bond for a certain amount (e.g., ₹2 Lakhs) to serve the bank for a minimum period of three years . If the candidate resigns before the completion of the bond period, they will have to pay the bond amount.

What is the career growth for an SBI PO? The career progression for an SBI PO is very fast. After probation, a PO is confirmed as an Assistant Manager. Subsequent promotions are to Deputy Manager, Manager, Chief Manager, and so on, up to the level of Chairman. SBI offers excellent opportunities for career advancement.

content: © 2026 Sandeep Kumar
Securities and Exchange Board of India - Assistant Manager (Information Technology)
About the Examination
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The SEBI Grade A (IT) exam is designed to select candidates with a strong technical foundation and the ability to apply their skills in a high-stakes regulatory environment. The selection process aims to identify individuals who possess:
Technical Expertise: Deep knowledge of core computer science and IT subjects like networking, databases, cybersecurity, and programming.
Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to analyze complex technical issues, design solutions, and troubleshoot problems in a mission-critical infrastructure.
General Aptitude: Foundational skills in quantitative aptitude, reasoning, and English, which are essential for any managerial role.
Awareness of Financial Markets: A basic understanding of the financial sector is beneficial, as the role involves supporting the technological backbone of the market regulator.
🏛️ The Role of an IT Officer in SEBI
An Assistant Manager in the IT stream at SEBI is responsible for a wide range of critical functions, including:
🪜 The Three-Stage Selection Process
The selection process is a rigorous three-tiered structure designed to holistically evaluate a candidate's suitability.

Stage 1: Phase I (Online Screening Test): This is a qualifying examination consisting of two papers. Paper 1 tests general aptitude, while Paper 2 focuses on specialized IT knowledge. Its primary purpose is to screen candidates for the next phase.

Stage 2: Phase II (Online Examination): Candidates who clear Phase I appear for this stage. It also consists of two papers: Paper 1 is a descriptive English test, and Paper 2 is an advanced test of IT knowledge. The marks from Phase II are given high weightage in the final merit list.
Stage 3: Interview: Candidates who clear the Phase II cut-off are shortlisted for a personal interview. The interview assesses technical knowledge, personality, and suitability for a regulatory body.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allocation

The final merit list is prepared by assigning a weightage of 85% to the marks obtained in Phase II and 15% to the marks obtained in the Interview . Successful candidates are offered the position of Assistant Manager (Grade A) and undergo a probationary period, typically of two years.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)
The SEBI Grade A recruitment cycle is not fixed annually, but when it occurs, it typically spans 4-6 months from notification to the final result. The following is an example timeline.
⚠️ Disclaimer: This timeline is indicative. SEBI's recruitment is not on a fixed annual calendar. Always refer to the official SEBI website for the latest notifications.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (e.g., March - April)
March: The official detailed notification is released on the SEBI website (sebi.gov.in).
March - April: The online application window remains open for approximately 3-4 weeks.
Phase 2: Phase I Examination (e.g., May)
May (Early): Call letters for the Phase I online examination are released.
May (Mid/Late): The Phase I online examination is conducted on a single day across various centers.
Phase 3: Phase I Result & Phase II Examination (e.g., June - July)
June: The results of the Phase I examination are declared, and a list of shortlisted candidates is published.
July (Early): Call letters for the Phase II online examination are released.
July (Mid/Late): The Phase II online examination is conducted.
Phase 4: Interview & Final Result (e.g., August - September)
August: Results of Phase II are declared, and a list of candidates shortlisted for the interview is released. Interview call letters are sent out.
August/September: Interviews are conducted, usually at the SEBI Head Office in Mumbai.
September: The final result, based on combined Phase II and interview scores, is published.
Eligibility Criteria
Candidates must strictly adhere to the eligibility criteria regarding nationality, age, and educational qualifications as specified in the official notification.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate must be a citizen of India.
🎂 2. Age Limit

A candidate must not have exceeded the age of 30 years as on the date specified in the notification (e.g., March 31, 2025). This means the candidate must have been born on or after the corresponding date (e.g., April 01, 1995).
🎓 3. Educational Qualification (for IT Stream)
A candidate must possess one of the following qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Electrical / Electronics / Electronics and Communication / Information Technology / Computer Science) from a recognized University / Institute. OR
Masters in Computers Application (MCA) from a recognized University / Institute. OR
Bachelor’s Degree in any discipline with a post-graduate qualification (minimum 2 years duration) in Computers / Information Technology from a recognized University / Institute.
Note: A candidate appearing for the final year/semester of their degree can also apply, provided they can produce proof of passing the examination by the date specified in the official notification.
✍️ 4. Number of Attempts
There is no restriction on the number of attempts for the SEBI Grade A examination, provided the candidate fulfills the age and educational criteria.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The selection process for SEBI Grade A (IT) is a three-stage process: Phase I, Phase II, and an Interview. All papers (except English Descriptive) will be available in both English and Hindi.
🎯 Phase I: Online Screening Examination
Phase I is an online examination consisting of two objective-type papers. To be shortlisted for Phase II, a candidate must clear the individual cut-offs for each paper and the aggregate cut-off.
Negative Marking: There will be a penalty of 1/4th of the marks assigned to the question for each wrong answer in both papers.
📝 Phase II: Online Examination
Candidates shortlisted from Phase I will appear for Phase II. The marks from this phase are crucial for the final selection.
Negative Marking: There will be a penalty of 1/4th of the marks for wrong answers in Paper 2.
🗣️ Stage 3: Interview
Candidates who clear the aggregate cut-off in Phase II will be called for an interview. The interview can be conducted in either Hindi or English, at the candidate's choice.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the candidate's performance in Phase II and the Interview. The weightage is as follows:
Marks obtained in Phase II Examination: 85% Weightage
Marks obtained in Interview: 15% Weightage
Application Workflow
The application process is conducted entirely online through the official SEBI website.
Step 1: Registration: Candidates must visit the SEBI careers page and click on the link for new registration. They need to provide a valid email ID and mobile number.
Step 2: Filling the Application Form: Fill in personal, academic, and other details carefully.
Step 3: Document Upload: Upload a recent photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and a handwritten declaration as per the specifications given in the notification.
Step 4: Fee Payment: The application fee (e.g., ₹1000 for General/OBC/EWS and ₹100 for SC/ST/PwBD) must be paid online.
Step 5: Final Submission: After verifying all details, submit the application form and take a printout for future reference.
Syllabus
The syllabus for the SEBI Grade A (IT) exam covers a broad range of topics from general aptitude to specialized technical subjects.
📚 Phase I - Paper 1 Syllabus (Common to all streams)

Quantitative Aptitude: Number Series, Simplification/Approximation, Quadratic Equations, Data Interpretation (Bar, Pie, Line, Tabular), Time & Work, Speed Time & Distance, Profit & Loss, Simple & Compound Interest, Ratio & Proportion, Percentage, Averages.
Test of Reasoning: Puzzles, Seating Arrangements, Syllogism, Blood Relations, Direction Sense, Inequality, Coding-Decoding, Logical Reasoning.
English Language: Reading Comprehension, Cloze Test, Para Jumbles, Spotting Errors, Fill in the Blanks, Sentence Improvement, Vocabulary (Synonyms/Antonyms).
General Awareness: Current Affairs (especially related to the financial sector), Static GK, Banking & Insurance Awareness, Economy, Government Schemes, Books & Authors, Important Days.
✒️ Phase II - Paper 1 Syllabus (English Descriptive)
Essay Writing: Topics will often be related to finance, technology, economy, or social issues.
Précis Writing: Summarizing a given passage to about one-third of its length.
Reading Comprehension: Answering questions based on a given passage.
💻 Phase I & II - Paper 2 Syllabus (Information Technology)
The syllabus for Paper 2 is the same for both phases, but the difficulty level is higher in Phase II.
Database Concepts & SQL: ER-diagrams, normalization, transaction management, concurrency control, SQL queries.
Data Structures & Algorithms: Array, Linked List, Stack, Queue, Tree, Hash Table, Graph. Searching and Sorting algorithms, Time & Space complexity analysis.
Programming Concepts: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles using C++ or Java, basic control structures, functions, pointers (C/C++), exception handling.
Computer Networks: OSI & TCP/IP models, IP addressing (IPv4/IPv6), routing protocols, TCP/UDP, DNS, HTTP, network security basics (firewalls, IDS/IPS).
Operating System: Processes, threads, memory management, file systems, CPU scheduling, deadlocks, concurrency and synchronization.
Software Engineering: Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) models (Waterfall, Agile), software design principles, testing methodologies.
Information & Cyber Security: Cryptography basics (symmetric/asymmetric), network security protocols (SSL/TLS), common vulnerabilities & attacks (SQL Injection, XSS), security governance.
Data Analytics: Introduction to Data Warehousing, Big Data concepts, basics of languages like R and Python for data analysis.
Shell Programming: Basic Linux/Unix commands and shell scripting.
Frequently Asked Questions
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Application

Can a final-year B.Tech student apply for the exam? Yes. Final-year students can apply, but they must be able to produce the final degree/mark sheet by the cut-off date mentioned in the official SEBI notification.

Is a Master's degree compulsory for IT Officer? No. A B.E./B.Tech in the specified engineering disciplines is sufficient. MCA or a Post-Graduate qualification in Computers/IT are alternative qualifications.
❓ Regarding the Examination
Is there sectional timing in Phase I, Paper 1? No. There is a composite time of 60 minutes for the four sections in Paper 1. Candidates can switch between sections.
What is the negative marking scheme? Yes. For every wrong answer in the objective papers (Phase I & Phase II Paper 2), 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question will be deducted.
Are there coding questions in the IT paper? No. The IT paper (Paper 2) consists of Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) only. There are no practical coding or programming questions.
Are the marks of Phase I considered for the final merit list? No. Phase I is only for screening. The final merit list is based on Phase II marks (85% weightage) and Interview marks (15% weightage).

content: © 2026 Sandeep Kumar
Staff Selection Commission - Combined Graduate Level Examination
About the Examination

The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) Combined Graduate Level (CGL) Examination is a prominent national-level exam conducted to recruit personnel for Group ‘B’ (Non-Gazetted) and Group ‘C’ (Non-Technical) posts in various Ministries, Departments, and Organizations of the Government of India. It is one of the most sought-after examinations for graduates in India, offering a stable and prestigious career in the central government workforce.
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The SSC CGL exam is structured to select candidates who possess strong foundational knowledge and aptitude required for administrative and executive roles. The core philosophy is to identify individuals who demonstrate:
Quantitative & Analytical Skills: The ability to work with numbers, interpret data, and solve problems logically.
Reasoning Ability: The capacity for logical deduction, pattern recognition, and critical thinking.
Language Proficiency: Strong comprehension and communication skills, particularly in English.
General Awareness: A good understanding of the static and current events shaping the world, with a focus on India.
Adaptability: Suitability for a wide range of roles, from clerical and fieldwork to audit and analysis.
🏛️ The Posts and Services at Stake
Successful candidates are allocated to various posts based on their rank and preferences. These posts are categorized by their Pay Level in the 7th Central Pay Commission.
1. Group ‘B’ Gazetted Posts (Pay Level-8):
2. Group ‘B’ Non-Gazetted Posts (Pay Level-7 & 6):
3. Group ‘C’ Posts (Pay Level-5 & 4):
🪜 The Two-Tiered Selection Process
The CGL is a multi-stage process where each tier serves a specific purpose in filtering and selecting the most competent candidates.

Stage 1: Tier-I Examination (The Qualifying Filter): This is an objective-type, computer-based screening test. With lakhs of applicants, its primary role is to shortlist candidates for the next stage. It tests the breadth of a candidate's aptitude across four key areas: Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude, and English. Crucially, the marks from this stage are not counted for the final merit list. It is only qualifying in nature.

Stage 2: Tier-II Examination (The Merit Decider): Candidates who clear Tier-I undertake the Tier-II Examination, which is the decisive stage. It is also a computer-based test that evaluates a candidate's subject-specific knowledge and skills in greater depth. The marks from the Tier-II Examination are the sole determinant of the final score and rank . This stage also includes qualifying tests for computer knowledge and data entry speed.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allocation

The final merit list is prepared based on the overall performance in the Tier-II Examination . Based on their final rank, the post preferences submitted by them, their category, and the available vacancies, candidates are allocated to a specific post and department. This final allocation marks the successful entry into a coveted central government job.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)

The SSC CGL examination cycle typically spans 8-10 months from notification to the final result. Aspirants should be prepared for a sustained period of preparation. The following is a general, indicative schedule.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official SSC calendar and notification for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (June - July)

June: The official notification for the CGL Examination is released by SSC on its website (ssc.nic.in). This document contains all vital information: post details, vacancies, eligibility, syllabus, and exam pattern.

June - July: The online application window opens on the day of notification and remains active for about one month . This involves using the One-Time Registration (OTR) portal to fill out the application form.
Phase 2: Tier-I Examination (August - September)
August: Approximately 1-2 weeks before the exam date , SSC releases the Application Status and e-Admit Card for the Tier-I Examination on its regional websites.
August / September: The Tier-I computer-based examination is conducted in multiple shifts over several days across the country.
Phase 3: Tier-I Result & Answer Key (October - November)
September: A few days after the exam concludes, the tentative Answer Key is released, and candidates can raise objections.
October / November: The results of the Tier-I Examination are declared, along with the category-wise cut-off marks. A list of qualified candidates is published.
Phase 4: Tier-II Examination (December)
November / December: Admit cards for the Tier-II Examination are released for all shortlisted candidates.
December: The Tier-II Examination is conducted. This is also a computer-based test and is typically held on a single day for most candidates.
Phase 5: Final Result and Post Allocation (February - March of next year)
January: The tentative Answer Key for Tier-II is released.
February: The final result, based on Tier-II scores, is declared. This includes a merit list of all successful candidates.
March onwards: The process of document verification and allocation of posts and departments to the selected candidates is carried out by the user departments.
Eligibility Criteria

Aspirants must carefully check their eligibility for the SSC CGL examination. The criteria set by the Staff Selection Commission are mandatory. Eligibility is determined by Nationality, Age Limit, and Educational Qualification.
⚠️ Note: The details provided here are based on prevailing rules. These are subject to change, and the official SSC notification for the current examination year is the ultimate authority.
🌍 1. Nationality
A candidate must be either:
(a) a citizen of India, or
(b) a subject of Nepal, or
(c) a subject of Bhutan, or
(d) a Tibetan refugee who came over to India, before the 1st January 1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or

(e) a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, East African Countries of Kenya, Uganda, the United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia and Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India.
Candidates belonging to categories (b), (c), (d) and (e) must possess a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India.
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age limit for SSC CGL varies for different posts. The age is calculated as of a specific cut-off date, typically the 1st of August of the examination year.
For posts with age limit 18-27 years: Candidate must have been born not earlier than 02-08-1998 and not later than 01-08-2007 (for CGL 2025, as an example).
For posts with age limit 20-30 years: Candidate must have been born not earlier than 02-08-1995 and not later than 01-08-2005.
For posts with age limit 18-30 years: Candidate must have been born not earlier than 02-08-1995 and not later than 01-08-2007.
For posts with age limit 18-32 years: Candidate must have been born not earlier than 02-08-1993 and not later than 01-08-2007.
SSC provides relaxations in the upper age limit for reserved categories:
🎓 3. Educational Qualification
The minimum educational qualification for most posts is a Bachelor's Degree.
For All Posts (except AAO and JSO): A Bachelor's Degree from a recognized University or equivalent.

For Assistant Audit Officer/Assistant Accounts Officer (AAO): Essential: Bachelor's Degree from a recognized University. Desirable: Chartered Accountant or Cost & Management Accountant or Company Secretary or Masters in Commerce or Masters in Business Studies or Masters in Business Administration (Finance) or Masters in Business Economics.
Essential: Bachelor's Degree from a recognized University.

Desirable: Chartered Accountant or Cost & Management Accountant or Company Secretary or Masters in Commerce or Masters in Business Studies or Masters in Business Administration (Finance) or Masters in Business Economics.

For Junior Statistical Officer (JSO): Bachelor's Degree in any subject from a recognized University or Institute with at least 60% Marks in Mathematics at 12th standard level; OR Bachelor's Degree in any subject with Statistics as one of the subjects at degree level.
Bachelor's Degree in any subject from a recognized University or Institute with at least 60% Marks in Mathematics at 12th standard level; OR
Bachelor's Degree in any subject with Statistics as one of the subjects at degree level.

Final-Year Students: Candidates who are in the final year of their graduation can also apply, however, they must possess the essential qualification on or before the cut-off date specified in the official notice.
✍️ 4. Number of Attempts

There is no limit on the number of attempts a candidate can take for the SSC CGL examination. A candidate may appear for the examination as many times as they wish, provided they satisfy all other eligibility conditions, including the age limit for their desired post(s).
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The SSC CGL examination is conducted in two tiers. A thorough understanding of the pattern and marking scheme of both tiers is essential for a focused preparation strategy.
🎯 Tier-I Examination (Qualifying Nature)

The Tier-I exam is a computer-based objective test designed to screen candidates for the next stage. Its marks are not counted for the final merit list, but candidates must clear the category-wise cut-off to be eligible for Tier-II.
Total Duration: 1 hour (60 minutes). 80 minutes for PwBD candidates.
Question Type: Objective Type, Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs).
Language: The questions will be set in both English & Hindi, except for the English Comprehension part.
Negative Marking: There is a penalty of 0.50 marks for each incorrect answer.
📝 Tier-II Examination (Merit Deciding Stage)
This is the final and most crucial stage. The final merit list and post allocation depend entirely on the scores obtained in Tier-II. It consists of three separate papers.
Negative Marking: For Paper-I: 1 mark is deducted for each wrong answer. For Paper-II & Paper-III: 0.50 marks are deducted for each wrong answer.
For Paper-I: 1 mark is deducted for each wrong answer.
For Paper-II & Paper-III: 0.50 marks are deducted for each wrong answer.

Qualifying Sections: The Computer Knowledge Test (CKT) and Data Entry Speed Test (DEST) are mandatory but qualifying in nature. Candidates must clear the minimum cut-off in these to be considered for the final merit list.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the overall performance in Tier-II. The scores are calculated as follows:
For posts other than JSO & AAO: Marks scored in Section-I & Section-II of Paper-I. (Total 390 Marks)
For JSO: Marks from Paper-I + Marks from Paper-II. (Total 590 Marks)
For AAO: Marks from Paper-I + Marks from Paper-III. (Total 590 Marks)
Application Workflow
The application process for SSC CGL is entirely online through the new official portal (ssc.gov.in) . The process requires careful attention to detail to avoid rejection.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)
This is a mandatory, one-time activity for all aspirants. Once completed, your basic details are saved for all future SSC examinations.
Purpose: OTR saves a candidate's personal details, contact information, and declaration, which are automatically fetched when applying for an exam.
Information Required: You will need personal details (Aadhaar, Name, Father's Name, Mother's Name, DOB), contact details (Mobile Number, Email ID), and Class 10 Board details.
Verification: Mobile number and email ID are verified via OTP. Use personal and active contact details for all SSC communications.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Examination Application Form
After OTR, log in to the SSC portal, navigate to the live examinations, and select the Combined Graduate Level Examination.
Personal Information: Verify the data auto-filled from your OTR profile.
Educational Qualification: Fill in the details of your highest qualification and your graduation degree.
Preference for Examination Centres: Select three examination centres in order of preference within the same region.

Syllabus
The SSC CGL syllabus outlines the topics candidates need to cover for each section of the Tier-I and Tier-II examinations.
The official notification from SSC is the final authority on the syllabus. The following is a detailed breakdown.
📚 Part A: Tier-I Examination Syllabus

Includes questions of both verbal and non-verbal type. Topics include analogy, symbolic operations, number/letter series, Venn diagrams, classification, syllogism, coding-decoding, problem-solving, emotional/social intelligence, embedded figures, etc.

Questions are designed to test the candidate’s general awareness of the environment around him and its application to society. Topics include India and its neighboring countries, History, Culture, Geography, Economic Scene, General Policy, and scientific research. Emphasis is on current events.

Questions are designed to test the ability of appropriate use of numbers and number sense. Topics include Whole numbers, Decimals, Fractions, Percentages, Ratio & Proportion, Square roots, Averages, Interest, Profit and Loss, Discount, Partnership, Mixture and Alligation, Time and distance, Time & Work, Basic algebraic identities, Graphs of Linear Equations, Triangle, Quadrilaterals, Circles, Trigonometry, Height and distances, Histogram, Frequency polygon, Bar diagram & Pie chart.

Candidates’ ability to understand correct English, their basic comprehension and writing ability would be tested. Topics include spotting the error, fill in the blanks, synonyms/antonyms, spelling/detecting mis-spelt words, idioms & phrases, one-word substitution, improvement of sentences, active/passive voice, direct/indirect narration, shuffling of sentence parts, cloze passage & comprehension passage.
✒️ Part B: Tier-II Examination Syllabus
The Tier-II syllabus is an extension of the Tier-I syllabus, with a higher difficulty level.

Module-I (Mathematical Abilities): Number Systems, Fundamental arithmetical operations, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Trigonometry, Statistics and Probability. The scope is wider and deeper than Tier-I.
Module-II (Reasoning and General Intelligence): Same topics as Tier-I, but with more complex questions.

Module-I (English Language and Comprehension): Vocabulary, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, and its correct usage; reading comprehension (including multiple passages), cloze test, para jumbles.
Module-II (General Awareness): Same topics as Tier-I, with a focus on recent current affairs (last 6-8 months).
Module-I (Computer Knowledge): Basics of Computer, Software, Working with Internet and e-mails, Basics of networking and cyber security.

Collection, Classification and Presentation of Statistical Data, Measures of Central Tendency, Measures of Dispersion, Moments, Skewness and Kurtosis, Correlation and Regression, Probability Theory, Random Variable and Probability Distributions, Sampling Theory, Statistical Inference, Analysis of Variance, Time Series Analysis, Index Numbers.

Part A: Finance and Accounts (80 marks): Fundamental principles and basic concept of Accounting. Part B: Economics and Governance (120 marks): Comptroller & Auditor General of India, Finance Commission, Basic Concept of Economics and introduction to Micro Economics, Theory of Demand and Supply, Theory of Production and cost, Forms of Market and price determination, Indian Economy, Economic Reforms in India, Money and Banking, Role of Information Technology in Governance.
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some of the most common questions aspirants have about the SSC CGL Examination.
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Attempts

Can I apply while in the final year of my graduation? Yes. You can apply provisionally, but you must be able to produce the final passing certificate on or before the cut-off date mentioned in the official notification.
Is there a limit on the number of attempts? No. There is no limit on attempts. You can appear for the exam as long as you fulfill the age criteria for the desired post.

Are the age limits the same for all posts? No. Different posts have different age group requirements (e.g., 18-27, 20-30, 18-32 years). You must check the specific age limit for each post you are interested in from the official notification.
❓ Regarding the Examination

Are the marks from Tier-I counted for the final merit list? No. As per the new pattern, Tier-I is only qualifying in nature. The final merit is prepared based on the marks scored in the Tier-II examination only.

Is normalization applied to the scores? Yes. Since the exams (both Tier-I and Tier-II) are conducted in multiple shifts, SSC uses a normalization formula to account for any variation in the difficulty level of the question papers across different shifts.

Is the Computer Knowledge Test (CKT) score added to the total? No. The CKT in Tier-II is mandatory for all posts but is qualifying in nature. You must score the minimum qualifying marks, but the score is not added to the final total for merit.
❓ Regarding Posts & Allocation
How do I give my post preferences? After the Tier-II result, SSC will activate a link for shortlisted candidates to submit their detailed Post Preferences online. This is a crucial step.

How are posts and departments allocated? Allocation is done strictly based on your rank in the final merit list (merit) and the order of posts you selected in your preference form (cum-preference), subject to you fulfilling the eligibility criteria for that post.

Is there an interview for any post in SSC CGL? No. The interview process for all posts under SSC CGL has been discontinued by the Government of India. The selection is based solely on the written examination performance.

content: © 2026 Sandeep Kumar
Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination
About the Examination
📜 The Philosophy Behind the Examination

The CHSL exam is meticulously designed to select individuals with strong clerical and operational aptitude, who form the foundational support system of the government machinery. The examination's core philosophy is to assess a candidate's suitability for roles that require precision, speed, and adherence to procedures. It aims to identify individuals who demonstrate:
Clerical Aptitude & Procedural Clarity: The ability to efficiently handle routine office tasks, manage files and data, and comprehend and follow official procedures.
Speed & Accuracy: A high degree of proficiency in typing and data entry, which is a critical, non-negotiable skill for the posts offered.
Basic Computer Proficiency: Foundational knowledge of computer operations, common office software (like MS Office), and internet usage.
Foundational Knowledge & Aptitude: A solid grasp of basic quantitative skills, logical reasoning, English language comprehension, and an awareness of the world around them.
🏛️ The Posts and Services at Stake
Successful candidates are recruited for essential clerical, secretarial, and data management roles that are the backbone of government administration. The primary posts are:
🪜 The Two-Tiered Selection Process
The CHSL selection is a two-stage process, with each tier serving a distinct purpose in filtering and selecting the most suitable candidates.

Stage 1: Tier-I Examination (The Great Filter): This is an objective, computer-based test that acts as a screening mechanism. Due to the massive number of applicants, its primary role is to shortlist a manageable number of candidates for the next, more intensive stage. It tests general aptitude across four core areas. Crucially, the marks from this stage are not counted for the final merit list; it is purely qualifying in nature.

Stage 2: Tier-II Examination (The Merit and Skill Decider): This is the final and most crucial stage. It is conducted in a single day and has multiple components. It includes an objective, computer-based test (whose marks determine the final merit) and mandatory qualifying tests for computer knowledge and data entry/typing skills. A candidate's final rank and selection depend entirely on their performance in the objective section of Tier-II.
🏆 The Final Verdict: Merit and Allocation

The final merit list is prepared based on the overall performance in the objective sections (Section-I and Section-II) of the Tier-II Examination . Based on their final rank, the post preferences submitted by them, their category, and the available vacancies, candidates are allocated to a specific post and department, marking their successful entry into the central government services.
Typical Timeline (Indicative)
The SSC CHSL examination cycle generally spans 8 to 10 months from notification to the final result. Aspirants must plan for a sustained period of preparation.
⚠️ Disclaimer: These timelines are based on past trends. Always refer to the official SSC calendar and notification for the specific year for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (April - May)
Early April: The official notification for the CHSL Examination is released by SSC on its website (ssc.gov.in), containing all crucial details like vacancies, eligibility, syllabus, and exam dates.
April - May: The online application window opens on the day of notification and remains active for about one month .
Phase 2: Tier-I Examination (July - August)
Early July: Approximately two weeks before the exam date, SSC releases the Application Status and e-Admit Cards for the Tier-I Examination on its regional websites.
July / August: The Tier-I computer-based examination is conducted in multiple shifts over several days across the country.
Phase 3: Tier-I Result & Answer Key (September - October)
Late August: A few days after the conclusion of the exam, the tentative Answer Key is released, and candidates are given a window to raise objections.
September / October: The results of the Tier-I Examination are declared. SSC publishes lists of candidates who have qualified for Tier-II.
Phase 4: Tier-II Examination (November - December)
Early November: Admit cards for the Tier-II Examination are released for all shortlisted candidates.
Late November / Early December: The Tier-II Examination (Objective Test + Skill/Typing Test) is conducted, typically on a single day for all candidates.
Phase 5: Final Result and Post Allocation (February - March of next year)
January: After the Tier-II exam, SSC opens a window for qualified candidates to submit their detailed Post Preferences online. This is a mandatory step for final consideration.
February: The final result, based on the performance in Tier-II, is declared. This includes the final merit list of all selected candidates.
Eligibility Criteria

Aspirants must carefully check their eligibility for the SSC CHSL examination. The criteria set by the Staff Selection Commission are mandatory and are based on Nationality, Age Limit, and Educational Qualification.
⚠️ Note: The official SSC notification for the current examination year is the ultimate authority. The cut-off date for age and educational qualifications mentioned in it is final.
🌍 1. Nationality

A candidate must be either: (a) a citizen of India, or (b) a subject of Nepal, or (c) a subject of Bhutan, or a person under other specified categories who possesses a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India.
🎂 2. Age Limit
The age limit for all posts under SSC CHSL is standard. The age is calculated as of a specific cut-off date, typically the 1st of August of the examination year.
Age Bracket: A candidate must be between 18 and 27 years of age.
This means a candidate must have been born not earlier than 02-08-1998 and not later than 01-08-2007 (for the 2025 exam, as an example).
SSC provides relaxations in the upper age limit for reserved categories as per government norms:
🎓 3. Educational Qualification
The minimum educational qualification for the CHSL exam is passing the 12th standard, with a specific requirement for one type of post.

For Lower Division Clerk (LDC) / Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA) and Data Entry Operator (DEO): Candidates must have passed the 12th Standard or an equivalent examination from a recognized Board or University.

For Data Entry Operator (DEO) Grade ‘A’ in the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG), Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, and Ministry of Culture: Candidates must have passed the 12th Standard in the Science stream with Mathematics as a subject from a recognized Board or equivalent.

Final-Year Students: Candidates who have appeared for their 12th Standard or equivalent examination can also apply. However, they must possess the essential qualification on or before the cut-off date specified in the official notice.
Stages, Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme

The SSC CHSL examination is a two-tier process. The final merit list is prepared based exclusively on the scores from the objective section of Tier-II, provided the candidate qualifies in all other mandatory tests.
🎯 Tier-I Examination (Qualifying Nature)
This is a computer-based screening test. Its marks are not counted for the final merit, and it serves only to shortlist candidates for Tier-II.
Total Duration: 1 hour (60 minutes). 80 minutes for PwBD candidates.
Question Type: Objective Type, Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs).
Language: Questions are set in both English & Hindi, except for the English Language part.
Negative Marking: There is a penalty of 0.50 marks for each incorrect answer.
📝 Tier-II Examination (Merit Deciding Stage)
This crucial stage consists of multiple sections and modules, including merit-deciding objective tests and mandatory qualifying skill tests, conducted in two separate sessions on the same day.
Merit Sections: Final merit is based *only* on the total marks of Section-I and Section-II.
Marking Scheme: For Section-I, Section-II, and Module-I of Section-III, each correct answer fetches +3 marks .
Negative Marking: There is a penalty of 1 mark for each incorrect answer in the objective tests of Tier-II.

Qualifying Sections: The Computer Knowledge Test and the Skill/Typing Test are mandatory for all candidates but are qualifying in nature. Failure to clear these will lead to disqualification, regardless of the score in merit sections.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
The final merit list is prepared based on the cumulative score of the two merit-deciding sections of Tier-II.
Total Marks in Section-I (out of 180) + Total Marks in Section-II (out of 180) = Grand Total for Merit: 360 Marks
Application Workflow
The application process for SSC CHSL is conducted exclusively online through the official SSC portal (ssc.gov.in) . The process requires careful attention to detail to avoid rejection.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)
This is a mandatory, one-time activity for all aspirants. Once completed, your basic details are saved for all future SSC examinations, simplifying the application process.
Information Required: You will need personal details (Aadhaar, Name, Father's Name, Mother's Name, DOB), contact details (Mobile Number, Email ID), and Class 10 Board details.
Verification: Mobile number and email ID are verified via OTP. Use personal and active contact details for all SSC communications.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Examination Application Form
After OTR, log in to the SSC portal, navigate to the live examinations, and select the Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination.
Personal Information: Verify the data auto-filled from your OTR profile.
Educational Qualification: Fill in the details of your 12th standard examination.
Preference for Examination Centres: Select three examination centres in order of preference.

Fee Payment: Amount: A non-refundable fee of ₹100 . Exemptions: Women candidates and candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen (ESM) categories are exempted . Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online through BHIM UPI, Net Banking, or by using Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, RuPay Credit or Debit cards.
Amount: A non-refundable fee of ₹100 .
Exemptions: Women candidates and candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen (ESM) categories are exempted .
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online through BHIM UPI, Net Banking, or by using Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, RuPay Credit or Debit cards.

Photograph and Signature Upload: Scanned Photograph: Must be a recent passport-size colour picture (not more than 3 months old), without cap and spectacles, with both ears clearly visible. Format: JPEG/JPG. Size: 20 KB to 50 KB. Scanned Signature: Must not be blurred. Format: JPEG/JPG. Size: 10 KB to 20 KB.
Scanned Photograph: Must be a recent passport-size colour picture (not more than 3 months old), without cap and spectacles, with both ears clearly visible. Format: JPEG/JPG. Size: 20 KB to 50 KB.
Scanned Signature: Must not be blurred. Format: JPEG/JPG. Size: 10 KB to 20 KB.
✅ Stage 3: Final Submission and Post-Submission Actions
Review and Submit: Before final submission, carefully review the entire application form in the preview section. After submission, no changes are possible outside the correction window.
Download Application PDF: After submission, download the filled application form and keep a copy for your records.
Application Form Correction Window: SSC provides a specific window (usually 2-3 days) after the application deadline closes to allow candidates to correct their forms by paying a correction charge.
Syllabus
The syllabus for the CHSL exam is based on the curriculum up to the 10th and 12th standards. The Tier-II syllabus is an extension of Tier-I with a slightly higher difficulty level.
📚 Tier-I Syllabus

General Intelligence: Includes questions of both verbal and non-verbal type. Topics include semantic analogy, symbolic operations, symbolic/number analogy, trends, figural analogy, space orientation, Venn diagrams, number series, coding and de-coding, problem-solving, etc.

General Awareness: Questions are designed to test the candidate’s general awareness of the environment and its application to society. Topics include India and its neighboring countries, especially pertaining to History, Culture, Geography, Economic Scene, General policy, and scientific research.

Quantitative Aptitude: Number Systems, Fundamental arithmetical operations, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Trigonometry, Statistical Charts (Use of Tables and Graphs: Histogram, Frequency polygon, Bar-diagram, Pie-chart).

English Language: Spot the Error, Fill in the Blanks, Synonyms/Homonyms, Antonyms, Spellings/Detecting mis-spelt words, Idioms & Phrases, One-word substitution, Improvement of Sentences, Active/Passive Voice of Verbs, Conversion into Direct/Indirect narration, Shuffling of Sentence parts, Cloze Passage, Comprehension Passage.
✒️ Tier-II Syllabus

Mathematical Abilities: Same topics as Tier-I but with more depth. Includes Number Systems, Fundamental arithmetical operations, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Trigonometry, and Statistics & Probability.
Reasoning and General Intelligence: Same topics as Tier-I with questions of higher complexity and depth.
English Language and Comprehension: Vocabulary, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms; Reading comprehension (based on a variety of passages), Cloze test, Para jumbles.
General Awareness: Same topics as Tier-I, but with a stronger emphasis on recent current affairs.
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are answers to some of the most common questions aspirants have about the SSC CHSL Examination.
❓ Regarding Eligibility & Posts

Can a student from an Arts or Commerce background apply for the post of DEO in C&AG? No. The post of Data Entry Operator (Grade 'A') in specified departments like C&AG specifically requires a 12th standard pass in the Science stream with Mathematics as a subject. Other candidates are not eligible for this specific post.

Is there any minimum percentage required in the 12th standard to apply? No. SSC does not specify any minimum percentage for eligibility. A candidate only needs to have passed the 12th standard examination from a recognized board.
❓ Regarding the Examination

Are the marks from Tier-I counted for the final merit list? No. As per the new pattern, Tier-I is only for screening/shortlisting candidates. The final merit list is prepared based on marks from Tier-II's objective sections (Section-I and Section-II) only.

What is the difference between the Skill Test and the Typing Test in Tier-II? The Skill Test is for DEO posts and requires a data entry speed of 8,000 Key Depressions per hour on a computer. The Typing Test is for LDC/JSA posts and requires a typing speed of 35 words per minute (w.p.m.) in English or 30 w.p.m. in Hindi. Both are qualifying in nature.

Is the Computer Knowledge Test scoring? No. The Computer Knowledge Test in Tier-II is mandatory for all but is qualifying in nature. You must clear its minimum cut-off, but its marks are not added to the final merit score.

Is there a separate cut-off for each section in Tier-II? Yes. SSC may prescribe separate cut-offs for different sections of Tier-II. A candidate has to clear the overall cut-off as well as the sectional cut-offs to be considered for the final merit list.

content: © 2026 Sandeep Kumar
Staff Selection Commission Junior Engineer Examination
About the Examination

The Staff Selection Commission Junior Engineer (SSC JE) Examination is a major national-level exam for recruiting Junior Engineers, who are Group ‘B’ (Non-Gazetted) technical staff. This exam is a fantastic opportunity for both Diploma holders and Engineering Graduates to secure a government job that's central to building and maintaining India's infrastructure. It's a role that puts you on the ground, applying your technical skills every day.
📜 What SSC Looks For
The SSC JE exam isn't just about formulas; it's about finding practical-minded engineers. It's designed to test your:
Core Engineering Knowledge: A solid grasp of the fundamentals of Civil, Mechanical, or Electrical engineering.
General Intelligence & Awareness: Strong reasoning skills and a good understanding of current events and general knowledge.
Practical Application: The ability to use your technical knowledge to solve real-world problems you'd face on a worksite.
🏛️ The Departments and Disciplines
Acing the SSC JE exam can land you a position in some of the most vital government organizations. Recruitment happens for three core engineering streams.
The three engineering disciplines are:
You could be working in prestigious organizations like:
🪜 The Selection Process
The selection process is straightforward and entirely based on written tests. There is no interview , making it a purely merit-based recruitment.

Paper-I (Computer Based Test): This is the first hurdle. It's an objective test that checks your reasoning, general awareness, and basic technical knowledge. Your score here is crucial for getting shortlisted for the next stage.

Paper-II (Computer Based Test): If you clear Paper-I, you'll take this test. It's also an objective CBT but focuses entirely on your specific engineering discipline. The questions are more in-depth and carry higher marks.

Document Verification (DV): Candidates are shortlisted based on their combined scores in Paper-I and Paper-II. If your name is on the list, you'll be called to verify your documents. That's the final step before you get your posting!
🏆 The Final Merit
Your final rank depends on the combined score of both written papers.
Normalized Marks in Paper-I (out of 200) + Normalized Marks in Paper-II (out of 300) = Final Merit Score (out of 500)
Typical Timeline (Indicative)
The SSC JE Exam follows a fairly regular annual schedule. As it's currently October 2025, the process for the 2025 exam would be in its final stages.
⚠️ Disclaimer: This is a typical schedule. Always check the official SSC calendar for exact dates.
Phase 1: Notification & Application (February - March)
The official notification usually comes out in late February, with the application window open for about a month.
Phase 2: Paper-I Exam (May - June)
The first computer-based test is typically held in late May or early June. Admit cards are available a week or two before the exam.
Phase 3: Paper-I Result (July - August)
SSC declares the Paper-I results and the cut-offs for each stream, shortlisting candidates for the next stage.
Phase 4: Paper-II Exam (September - October)
Paper-II is usually conducted a couple of months after the Paper-I results. Given the current date, this exam would have just concluded or be happening right now for the 2025 cycle.
Phase 5: Final Result & DV (December - January)
The final combined result is announced, and successful candidates are called for Document Verification, followed by the final allocation of departments.
Eligibility Criteria
Eligibility for SSC JE is very specific and can differ from one department to another. Always check the official notification for your chosen post.
🌍 1. Nationality
You must be a citizen of India (or meet other specific criteria for subjects of Nepal/Bhutan, etc., as per government rules).
🎓 2. Educational Qualification

You need either a B.E./B.Tech OR a 3-year Diploma in Civil, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering. Some departments may also require a specific amount of work experience, especially for Diploma holders. This is a crucial detail to check in the official advertisement.
🎂 3. Age Limit
The age limit varies by department. The cut-off date is usually the 1st of August of the notification year. Standard age relaxations apply for reserved categories (SC/ST: 5 years, OBC: 3 years).
Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
The SSC JE exam has two objective computer-based tests.
📝 Paper-I (Computer Based Test)
Duration: 2 Hours.
Negative Marking: Yes, -0.25 marks for each wrong answer.
🎯 Paper-II (Computer Based Test)
Negative Marking: Yes, -1 mark for each wrong answer.
Calculator: A virtual scientific calculator will be available on your screen.
📊 Final Rank Calculation
Your final selection depends on your combined performance in both papers after marks are normalized.
Paper-I Normalized Score (out of 200) + Paper-II Normalized Score (out of 300) = Final Merit Score (out of 500)
Application Workflow

The application process for the SSC JE examination is conducted entirely online through the new official SSC website (ssc.gov.in). It's a systematic process that requires careful attention to detail to avoid rejection. The workflow can be broken down into key stages.
📝 Stage 1: One-Time Registration (OTR)
Before you can apply for any SSC exam, you must complete the One-Time Registration. This is a one-time activity that simplifies future applications.

Purpose: OTR saves your basic personal information (name, address, educational qualifications) on the SSC portal. This data is auto-filled whenever you apply for an exam, saving time and preventing errors.
Information Required: You will need your Aadhaar card, Class 10th and 12th details, a valid mobile number, a valid email ID, and scanned copies of your photograph and signature.
Verification: Your mobile number and email ID will be verified using OTPs. Ensure these are personal and active, as all communications from SSC will be sent to them.
✍️ Stage 2: Filling the Application Form
Once your OTR is complete, you can log in to the SSC portal and apply for the "Junior Engineer (Civil, Mechanical & Electrical) Examination."
Personal Details: Most of your details will be automatically populated from your OTR profile. You will need to verify them.
Educational Qualifications: Provide the details of your Engineering Diploma or Degree.

Post Preferences: This is a critical step. You must carefully select and order your preferences for various departments (like CPWD, MES, BRO, etc.) that you are eligible for. This preference is final and is used for allocation after the results.
Examination Centre Selection: You will be asked to choose your preferred cities for the examination from a list of available centers.
💳 Stage 3: Fee Payment and Document Upload
1. Fee Payment:
Amount: A non-refundable application fee of ₹100 (Rupees One Hundred only).

Exemptions: Women candidates and candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), and Ex-Servicemen (ESM) are exempted from paying the fee.
Payment Modes: The fee can be paid online through BHIM UPI, Net Banking, or by using Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, or RuPay Credit/Debit cards.
2. Uploading of Photograph and Signature:
SSC has very strict specifications for the photograph and signature. Failure to comply can lead to application rejection.
Live Photograph: The new application process requires candidates to capture a live photograph through the webcam on their computer or mobile device. Ensure good lighting and a plain background.
Scanned Signature: The signature must be scanned clearly in the specified format (typically JPG/JPEG , with a size between 10 KB to 20 KB ).
✅ Stage 4: Final Submission and Post-Submission Actions

Review and Submit: Before the final submission, you will be shown a preview of your application. Review every detail for accuracy. Once submitted, changes are only possible during the 'Correction Window'.
Download Application PDF: After successful submission, download and print a copy of your application form for your records.

Application Correction Window: SSC provides a brief window (usually 2-3 days) after the application period closes to allow candidates to make corrections to their forms upon payment of a correction fee.
⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid
Last-Minute Rush: Applying on the last day can lead to server issues, payment failures, and mistakes. Apply early.
Incorrect Photo/Signature: Failing to meet the specific requirements for the live photograph or scanned signature is a common reason for rejection.
Wrong Post Preferences: Not filling the post preferences carefully can lead to you being allocated to a department you didn't want, even with a good rank.
Ignoring Eligibility: Applying for a post for which you do not meet the specific age or educational criteria mentioned in the notification.
Syllabus
The official notification from SSC is the final authority on the syllabus. The following is a detailed breakdown.
📚 Paper-I Syllabus
This section tests your logical thinking. Expect questions on analogies, similarities, differences, problem-solving, analysis, judgment, decision making, visual memory, and arithmetical reasoning.
This covers a broad range of topics including current events, India and its neighboring countries (History, Culture, Geography, Economy), General Polity, and Scientific Research.
✒️ General Engineering Syllabus (For Paper-I Part-C & Paper-II)
Building Materials: Properties, tests, and uses of building materials like stones, cement, concrete, steel.
Estimating, Costing and Valuation: Methods of estimation, analysis of rates, valuation principles.
Surveying: Principles, leveling, contouring, theodolite traversing, advanced surveying.
Soil Mechanics: Soil properties, classification, permeability, consolidation, shear strength, bearing capacity.
Hydraulics: Fluid mechanics, flow through pipes, open channel flow, turbines, and pumps.
Irrigation Engineering: Methods of irrigation, water requirements of crops, dams, canals.
Transportation Engineering: Highway and railway engineering, pavement design, traffic engineering.
Environmental Engineering: Water quality and treatment, sewage treatment, pollution.
Theory of Structures: Bending moments, shear force, stress-strain, trusses, columns.
Concrete Technology: Properties, mix design, quality control.
RCC & Steel Design: Design of beams, slabs, columns, footings, and basic steel structures.
Basic Concepts: Resistance, inductance, capacitance, current, voltage, power, energy.
Circuit Law & Magnetic Circuit: Kirchhoff’s laws, network theorems, concepts of flux, MMF, reluctance.
AC Fundamentals: Sinusoidal waveforms, R-L-C circuits, resonance, three-phase systems.
Measurement and Instruments: Ammeters, voltmeters, wattmeters, energy meters, bridges.
Electrical Machines: DC Machines, Transformers, Three-phase Induction motors, Synchronous machines.
Generation, Transmission & Distribution: Power stations, transmission line parameters, different distribution systems.
Estimation and Costing: Estimation of electrical installations, IE rules.
Utilization of Electrical Energy: Illumination, heating, welding, drives.
Basic Electronics: Diodes, Transistors (BJT, JFET), basic circuits.
Theory of Machines and Machine Design: Simple mechanisms, linkages, gears, belts, clutches, flywheels.
Engineering Mechanics and Strength of Materials: Equilibrium, friction, laws of motion, stress-strain, SFD & BMD, torsion.
Thermal Engineering: Laws of Thermodynamics, properties of substances, IC Engine cycles (Otto, Diesel), Rankine cycle, refrigeration.
Fluid Mechanics & Machinery: Fluid properties, statics, dynamics, Bernoulli’s theorem, hydraulic turbines, pumps.
Production Engineering: Manufacturing processes like casting, forming, welding, machining. Heat treatment of steel, machine tools.
Frequently Asked Questions
❓ Is a Diploma or B.Tech better for SSC JE?

Both are eligible for most posts. B.Tech graduates may find the in-depth concepts of Paper-II easier, while Diploma holders might have a practical edge. Success depends on your preparation, not just your qualification.
❓ Is there an interview for the SSC JE post?
No. The selection process is based entirely on the written tests (Paper-I and Paper-II). This is a huge plus for candidates who excel in written exams.
❓ How are the final marks calculated with two papers and multiple shifts?

SSC uses a process called **normalization**. Your raw scores in Paper-I and Paper-II are converted to a normalized score to account for differences in difficulty levels across various exam shifts. The final merit list is based on the sum of these normalized scores.
❓ Can I use my own calculator in Paper-II?
No. You are not allowed to bring a physical calculator. A virtual (on-screen) scientific calculator will be provided during the Paper-II Computer Based Test.
